title: The letters of thought, and the three levels of thought

lectures.id: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

overview: This class opens the letters of thought and the three levels of thought itself. *Bina* is the mother, and its garments, the five *gevuros*, appear as the letters of thought and speech. The five letters with final forms, the *mnatzpach*, are the *gevuros*, the limiting forces that divide an idea into parts. The seal (*pesuchei chotam*) is the source of the distinctions among the letters of thought, and words follow from the distinctions that understanding makes. The three levels are action of thought, which is imagining and picturing and which a small child has without words; speech of thought, which is words someone else has put into one's mind and is lower than real thought; and thought of thought, real thought, which is analysis that comes from understanding and will, and whose *kavana* shapes the words it finds. Thought depends on *daas*: a child has no thought of its own, and a person's thought is their own only when they take an idea in and express it in their own words. The class ends on the point that this is how a person is liberated, through *bina*.

sections.title: The garments of bina are the letters of thought
sections.summary: Bina's garments, the five gevuros, show up as the letters of thought: the seal makes the distinctions, and words follow from them.

phrases.he: והנה ידוע בענין המאמר דאימא אוזיפת מאנהא לברתא
phrases.en: So, it's known, the statement in the *Zohar*, that the mother lends her clothes to her daughter.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: And these garments are the five *gevuros*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: *Mnatzpach* are the letters, the five letters of the Hebrew alphabet that have a different form when they're at the end of a word.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: they're also called the engraving of the signet ring

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: חותם שהוא בחינת צרופי התחלקות אותיות דמחשבה,
phrases.en: And that becomes the source for these distinctions and the division between the letters of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב בזהר על פסוק וקול התור נשמע בארצנו
phrases.en: like it explains in the *Zohar*, about the verse, "and the voice of the dove will be heard in our land"

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: as explained elsewhere

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: We are still on the letters of thought, with the letters of speech coming soon. Line 1 rests on a known *Zohar* statement: the mother lends her clothes to her daughter.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The simple idea: *bina* (understanding) is the mother and *Malchus* the daughter. The garments of *bina*, its *levushim*, become expressed in the letters of thought and of speech.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: These garments are the five *gevuros* (the limiting forces of *bina*). *Mnatzpach* are the five letters that take a different form at the end of a word.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Each has a regular form and a closed or long final form: mem and final mem, nun and final nun, and so for all five. They are the five *gevuros* that cut an idea into distinct parts and create diversity.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The five are also called *pesuchei chotam*, the engraving of a signet ring. The seal is the source of the distinctions among the letters of thought: *bina* recognizes them in understanding itself, and words come afterwards. A distinction no one notices gets no word.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Words for colors and for different cultures
blocks.text: Cultures differ in how many words they have. Many languages have one word for blue and green, shades of one spectrum, and old Hebrew *yarok* can mean anything from yellow to green.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Specialized jargon
blocks.text: The same with jargon: a doctor needs words a layperson does not, a sailor says starboard and aft, a pilot talks of yaw and roll. Those words are meaningful in their context, but a layperson does not see the distinctions, since they are not relevant to daily life.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the basic idea. The *Zohar* explains it on the verse "and the voice of the *tor* (turtledove) will be heard in our land": the *tor* is like the masculine form of *Torah*. This comes up again; this chapter is only an introduction, and the five *gevuros* start in chapter 42.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Three levels within thought itself
sections.summary: Thought has three stages: thought of thought, speech of thought, and action of thought. The class names them before taking the first one.

phrases.he: ותחלה יש להקדים שיש ג' מדריגות במחשבה עצמה,
phrases.en: First, we need to have an introduction about the idea that there are three levels within thought itself.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: והוא בחינת מחשבה דמחשבה ודבור שבמחשבה
phrases.en: And these are the three aspects or stages of thought of thought, speech of thought, and action of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and the explanation of this is known

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: we already started explaining this in our general introduction to the idea of *osios*, in chapter 37

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: And there we talked about how both in thought and in speech there are three general stages

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Before the three levels are taken one at a time: there are three levels within thought itself, thought of thought, speech of thought, and action of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The explanation is known: it was started in chapter 37, under the general introduction to *osios*, where thought and speech each have three general stages. The class now comes to the first.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: The first level: imagination without letters
sections.summary: The first stage of thought is picture and imagination with no words. A small child has it; the child is not yet thinking in the full sense because thought needs conscious awareness. A child already draws distinctions and has wants, but its thought is not yet full thought. Imagining what one wants and its experiences is the start of thought, called action of thought. Action of thought is the imagining that goes with doing, reading and picturing things. A very small child has only imagination, like a dream, and is easily pulled from one thing to another.

phrases.he: כו', והוא כמו תינוק קטן שאין לו מחשבה בצירופי אותיות עדיין,
phrases.en: and it's like a little child that even a little baby has this type of thought, that a little child, even though they don't yet know a language

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: it's just they're envisioning, they're imagining the thing that they want.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: They have this picture of what they want, that's coming from the power of imagination.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הגם שנמצא גם בדמיון זה התחלקות חלקים,
phrases.en: and even though the truth is even in this imagination there's already a certain idea of *hischalkus*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: And so, therefore, even a little child can, at this stage of thought, is able to focus their thought to imagine a particular thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: but it's all just with a in imagination, with this kind of imagery

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's not called thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: in other words, you're not thinking, we don't say that you're thinking about the thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: אשר לזה אמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה כלל
phrases.en: and therefore we say, that a child doesn't have thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: There is just imagination without letters: a person experiences things and can picture them, an apple or a duck, with no words narrating them. Memories come up the same way, without narration.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A very small child has this kind of thought before knowing a language. It is not verbal, but it is real: a child knows its mother, wants her, and tells what it wants from what it does not. So a small child, or an animal that does not speak, is not without thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is only imagining, a picture of what one wants, and it comes from the power of imagination. Imagination takes experiences, imprints them, and can combine parts of memories, so a person can recall, "I had this before, and now I want it," and direct desire and focus toward it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even in imagination there is already *hischalkus*, division. When we perceive, we filter and choose what to focus on, and set other things aside as less important. A baby knows its mother's look and sound and tells a stranger apart, so already at this stage a child can focus its thought on one particular thing.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: An adult does the same when imagining or remembering: attention goes to one specific item, with a labeling and recognition of the difference between this and that, even though it is not verbal.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is all imagery, and it is not called thought. It is called thought only with metacognition, awareness that you are thinking. Someone dreaming or daydreaming is passive, like images imprinted by walking outside. Real thought is conscious: one turns an idea over and looks at it from this side and that, a deeper layer.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The phrase is borrowed from the legal rule that for some objects, such as *tumah* or *muktzeh*, what one intends to do with them settles their status: an object one meant to use before Shabbos can be *muktzeh* or not, depending on that intention. So the rule that a child has no thought means that it has only this first level.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: even when the child gets a little older

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ויש לו צירופי התחלקות אותיות במחשבה,

phrases.en: it's not fully formed letters and words and ideas

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: רק שיוכל לחשוב בצמצום בדבר הפרטי דוקא
phrases.en: even though they can focus their imagination and attention towards a certain thing

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו לחשוב במוחו בדבר מה שנותנים לו,
phrases.en: like a child can think about what you give them,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: so they can they can recognize the difference

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and we see the child, they're going to want this and they're not going to want something else

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: So you see that they want something, they don't want something else

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: as is known

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this is the beginning of thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: called the *ma'aseh* of *machshava*, right?

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even when a child grows a little, its thought is not yet fully formed letters, words or ideas. It can focus on one particular thing, but full thought waits until the child learns to speak.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A child can think about what is given to it and tell it apart from what is not. It wants one thing and pushes another away, and that distinction is already in its mind.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: A small child and the car seat
blocks.text: A small child hated being strapped in: as soon as the seat was clicked in, it cried and struggled, and as soon as it was taken out, it was fine. Small children have preferences, so clearly they think.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is the start of thought, called *ma'aseh shebemachshava*, action of thought: a person imagines what they want and pictures the physical experiences.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ובגדול היינו מה שחושב איך לעשות דבר
phrases.en: and in an adult, we also have this level,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: let's say if you a person was going to draw or they were going to write something,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: או שעולה במחשבתו כל מה שצריך לעשות בפועל ממש
phrases.en: or let's say a person is just thinking about their day, what I got to do, and they're imagining like okay, thinking I have to do this, I have to do that, and anything that they want to do.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וגם מה שמצייר אותיות הכתב במחשבה,
phrases.en: and this in a similar way if a person is reading and the letters that are written down are imprinted into their mind, so they're thinking about the words in front of them

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: or when a person's thinking about, you know, something in front of them, any physical thing,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: whether it's actually in front of them or they're just conjuring it up in their memory, like a fruit or a tree,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and the same thing with any other image.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's all called just action of thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ובקטן אין לו גם בחינת מחשבה זו,
phrases.en: in a very small child, they don't even have this ability to actively conjure up a thought,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: They just have an imagination, kind of like in a dream,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: (ועם כל זה הוא למעלה מדמיון החלומות כו')
phrases.en: but still, the thought of a child when they're awake and they want their bottle or they want their mother or they want their thing, that's still higher than a dream

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: In an adult too there is this level: when driving you think where you want to go, turn right here and left there. On autopilot you still imagine what you want to do.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Whenever you do something you first imagine what you want to do, such as the letters you want to put down when writing. There is a certain thought there, but it is not verbal.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person can write or draw with clear intention and still not think in words. Artists are often best in a flow state, since verbal thought gets in the way. So there is thought, but not analytical thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Or a person thinks about the day: what they have to do, that they have to do this and that, and whatever they want to do.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same holds for reading, where the printed letters are imprinted in the mind, and for any physical thing in front of us, or one conjured in memory, like a fruit, a tree, or any image. Close your eyes and imagine an apple: that is action of thought, neither verbal nor analytical.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A very small child does not even have this kind of thought: there is imagination, like a dream, where things come up without the child directing them, and no active control even over action of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: That is why a child is easily distracted: put something else in front of it, and it is suddenly thinking about that, and it cannot keep a train of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Still, the thought of a child who is awake and wants its bottle or its mother is higher than a dream, in which things simply happen to a person with even less active control.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Galus is a dream; the prophets' vision comes by imagination
sections.summary: The first level of thought is compared to a dream. Galus is like sleep, in which a person does not direct their thought, yet the essence still shines through and Torah connects the soul even unaware.

phrases.he: וכמו שכתוב במקום אחר בענין ביד הנביאים אדמה, בכח המדמה שבמחשבה בלבד
phrases.en: as explained elsewhere, that G-d appears to the prophets with the power of imagination,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: לפי שבשעת השינה לא נשאר רק חלק האחרון יותר, שהוא רק הדמיון שבמחשבה
phrases.en: during a dream, when a person is sleeping, that all of their intellect kind of goes away, and all that's left is this lowest aspect of thought, which is the power of imagination,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and this is why galus is compared to a dream

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: like it says, "We were like dreamers,"

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כו', אך הן מעין הרהורי ליבא
phrases.en: but yet, what a person thinks about during the what the dream is about is similar to what they thought about during the day,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: as explained elsewhere,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Galus is compared to a dream, and so is the first level of thought. In galus a person does not actively direct their life; things happen to them, and they ride the waves. Awake, a person can say, "This is who I am, and this is my mission," and direct their life toward it. That is the difference between a personal state of geulah and of galus, the idea of Pesach and *zman cheiruseinu*: real freedom is being awake to that.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: As explained elsewhere, "by the hand of the prophets I appear" means that G-d appears to the prophets through the power of imagination alone. That experience is like a dream or a vision.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is why most prophets fell asleep when they received a prophecy: it was higher than their conscious understanding. In sleep the intellect goes away and only the lowest aspect of thought remains, the power of imagination, with no conscious direction.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: "We were like dreamers": yet what a person thinks about by day shows up in the dream, so the essence still comes through. Torah and mitzvos connect to the *neshama* even when one is not aware of it, as explained elsewhere. That is the first level of thought, action of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Speech of thought: words that come from someone else
sections.summary: Speech of thought is the thinking of words that someone else has put in one's mind, from a parent, a teacher or a Rebbe, rather than words one has made one's own. It is lower than real thought. The same words can be thought as letters, heard from someone else, read from a siddur, or thought through by oneself. Only the last is one's own thought, and it depends on understanding.

phrases.he: ובחינת דבור שבמחשבה הוא כמו שחושב צירופי אותיות הדבור שמדבר זולתו
phrases.en: where a person is thinking words of thought, but they're not creating the words of thought, they're just, you're hearing somebody else speaking.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: so this is lower than real thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: a person is thinking for himself

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: when there's nobody there, it's different than when somebody's talking to you

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: In the *mashal*, these are our levels of awareness and thought; in the *nimshal*, our levels of awareness of G-dliness, how *hashgacha pratis* is revealed to us. I think it is worth pointing out that some of us see only that G-d acts and creates, without sensing the inner purpose: G-d wants us to do this, but we have no sense of what is behind it. Purim is an example: G-d seemed hidden until the end of the story, when it was revealed that He had orchestrated it all. The question is whether we see G-d's hand in everything.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Speech of thought is when a person thinks words of thought but does not create them: they hear someone else speak. This goes back to the child: as parents speak, they bring out the understanding the child already has, and their words teach it distinctions.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person who does not yet know what to do can ask what the Rebbe would tell them, or what this person would tell them, or learn *Shulchan Aruch* so that the words of *halacha* play in their head, or hear what their parents told them. That voice acts like a conscience.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person can also be moved by other things, when the words of another play in their head. You see many people who go out to protest a cause: they don't understand what they are doing, they were only told something, and that mantra gets into their head and moves them, though the words are not their own.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A jab at people who protest a cause, not named; the public text keeps the point and drops the protest.
sensitivity.publishable: A person can also be moved by other things, when the words of another play in their head. You see many people who act on a mantra they were given: they don't understand what they are doing, they were only told something, and that mantra gets into their head and moves them, though the words are not their own.

blocks.text: This is lower than real thought: a person repeats what they were told. *Chovos HaLevavos*, in *Shaar HaYichud*, speaks of people who think about G-d's unity in the *Shema* without really understanding it, so it is not their own thought. Thinking for oneself, with no one speaking, is different from hearing someone explain it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו כאשר חושב צירופי אותיות אדון עולם,
phrases.en: like, for example, if a person is thinking the words of *Adon Olam*, right,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הרי באופן צירוף מיוחד כזה עצמו, כאשר שומע במחשבתו דבור זולתו כשמדבר אדון עולם,
phrases.en: if a person is just let's say listening to somebody else reading

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: אין זה רק שנחקק אותיות הדיבור זולתו במחשבתו,
phrases.en: the other person's words are being imprinted into his mind, into his thoughts

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא למטה מאותיות אדון עולם שבמחשבת עצמו
phrases.en: and this is lower than the words of *Adon Olam* in the person's own thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: וכך כל מחשבה שחושב איך לדבר טרם שמדבר
phrases.en: where you're thinking what you're going to say before you say

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and then right away they speak.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: that's also called

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Take the words of *Adon Olam*. Seeing the letters in the book is action of thought; thinking them to yourself, with the song playing in your head, is only the letters of speech of thought. Only then can one really think about the *kavana*, what the words mean.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: If a person hears someone else say the same words, the other person's words are imprinted into the mind from outside, even when the mind is not speaking them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Reading from the *siddur*, a person can know the meaning of the words and think of G-d as the eternal Master who creates everything, before time and after time. Yet it is like somebody else telling a story.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person who does not understand it could not have written it, and cannot think about it beyond what is in the book. So the understanding is limited, and it comes from someone else telling it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is lower than the words of *Adon Olam* in one's own thought. Thinking for oneself that G-d is the eternal Master, and really understanding it, is a far deeper connection; so we connect to things at different depths, with different levels of *kavana*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: When we learn Torah, at first it is G-d's Torah. As the verse in chapter 1 says, one desires "the Torah of G-d" and toils in "His Torah" day and night. When a person has really mastered and understood it, it becomes their own Torah. Many people learn a *sicha* or a book and can repeat it, but they are only parroting someone else's words. Asked a question, they feel threatened, because they have no answer. Someone who really understands can explain the idea in their own words, in a different way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Speech of thought at a more inner level: before speaking, a person rehearses what they are going to say, choosing the words and hearing themselves speak in the mind. Then they say it right away; that too is called speech of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Speech of thought turns into thought: two directions, and one's own thought
sections.summary: Speech of thought and thought of speech pass into each other, from the outside in and from the inside out. Only thought of thought, a person's own understanding, cannot be handed over by someone else. Thought of thought is the real letters of thought: analysis that comes from understanding and will. Even words thought by oneself can be only speech of thought, if no kavana is in them.

phrases.en: but again it's a little bit more of a *pnimiyus* type of speech of thought because it's coming from the person.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: You can have it going from the bottom up or it can go from the top down.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: נעשה אופן המחשבה בעת שמתחיל לדבר,
phrases.en: that when a person thought about what they wanted to say and they decided what they want to say, that then becomes the way, like we say, the train of thought which they have to thinking about when they're actually speaking, when they start to speak.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and again *machshava* can also mean like *ratzon*, what they wanted in their thought, what they wanted to say.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: מה שאין כן המדריגה הג', שהוא מחשבה שבמחשבה, היינו מחשבת עצמו
phrases.en: but then the third level of thought, which is thought of thought, which is the person's own thought, this is the real thought where it's the person's own thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Speech of thought is a bit more inner, because it comes from the person. It goes in two directions: from the bottom up, or from the top down.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Iron, and the four maidservants
blocks.text: Elsewhere it says the third *Beis HaMikdash* will be built of *barzel*, iron, whose letters spell *Bilhah*, *Rachel*, *Zilpah* and *Leah*. That is going from the bottom up: *Rachel* is speech and *Leah* thought, and their maidservants are external words and thought, which the person does not own.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is how one teaches a child: first it repeats prayers without knowing the words, sometimes wrongly; then it knows the words and understands them, though not yet as its own; eventually it thinks the idea with its own understanding. That is bottom up; it can also go top down.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Speech within thought becomes thought within speech. A person thinks what they want to say, and in the middle of saying it, the inner purpose they had in mind shows itself. They lose the train of thought, ask what they were saying, remember it, and continue.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: When a person thinks about how to say something and decides what they want to say, that thinking becomes the train of thought they have while speaking. *Machshava* can also mean *ratzon*: what they wanted, in their thought, to say.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The third level, thought of thought, is the person's own thought. Someone else cannot give you a *machshava*; it has to come from your own understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כשחושב צירופי אותיות אדון עולם בלא דבור
phrases.en: this is where a person is thinking the words of *Adon Olam*, but not in speech,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: או כשחושב שאר ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים שנקרא אותיות המחשבה
phrases.en: or a person's thinking about anything else in different forms, that's called the real letters of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: אך גם בזה יש ב' מדריגות, הא' אשר גם הוא בכלל דבור שבמחשבה
phrases.en: even in this thought of thought there's two levels, one level is still really part of the speech of thought,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: והוא כאשר אינו חושב כלל את ההשכלה והכוונה שבאותיות אדון עולם וכהאי גוונא,
phrases.en: So again, even when somebody else isn't, you're not listening to somebody else speak, you're just thinking for yourself, so you could be thinking the words of *Adon Olam* without the understanding, but not from somebody else, just from yourself,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: The kavana is thinking about how G-d rules over everything and he's the master

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: רק צירופי האותיות דאל"ף דלי"ת שבאדון וכהאי גוונא
phrases.en: but a person isn't thinking about that kavana, they're just thinking the words of *Adon Olam*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הגם שהוא בלא דבור, שהוא למעלה משמיעת דבור אדון עולם כנזכר לעיל,
phrases.en: so really in each of these levels we have two levels

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: מכל מקום נקרא גם זה בשם דבור שבמחשבה
phrases.en: That's also called an aspect of speech of thought, where the person is just thinking the words of *Adon Olam* to themselves,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Thinking the words of *Adon Olam* without speech, and thinking about their meaning, is the real letters of thought: analyzing the idea, turning it over. It is creative, coming from understanding and *ratzon*; any idea thought in different forms works the same way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even within this thought of thought there are two levels. The first is still part of speech of thought: a person thinks the words of *Adon Olam* without their understanding, not from someone else but from oneself. That is the idea of rulership and lordship. The *kavana* is thinking how G-d rules over everything and is the Master, but the person does not think that *kavana*; they only think the words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Even without speech, above hearing the words of *Adon Olam* from someone else, each of the three levels has two levels: one passive and coming from outside, one more inner and coming from oneself. In thought of thought, a person can think the words by heart, without the *kavana*, and that is still called speech of thought, its more inner aspect.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Speech of angels, and real thought shaped by kavana
sections.summary: The angels speak as thought speaks to thought, without sound. Real thought analyzes an idea's understanding, and the kavana in the mind shapes which words come out.

phrases.he: (וכענין וקרא זה אל זה, כמו באותיות המחשבה שלנו,
phrases.en: that the angels speak to each other and their speech is like our thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהיה יכול אדם לקרוא לזולתו בשמו במחשבה מה שקוראו בדבור,
phrases.en: like as if you could speak to somebody else by just thinking, like telepathically, you could call out to them in your mind, just like you do in speech.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כך הוא בחינת דבור של המלאכים
phrases.en: and that's the way the angels speak.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and the same thing it talks about in *Berachos* about the two souls that were speaking to each other.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: עם זה, שאינו נשמע לאדם כו'
phrases.en: So that communication is like speech of thought, which is not heard to a person

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: as explained elsewhere

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: and the second level, which is real thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא מה שחושב את ההשכלה של הענין
phrases.en: where a person is thinking about the *kavana*

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שבאותיות המחשבה, שמחמתו הוא חושב מיד אופן הצירופים של אותיות הללו
phrases.en: and that's why these words or another, the words of their thought are being created from the analysis.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The angels speak to one another as we call out in thought. A person could call someone by name in their mind, by thinking alone, and even a person screaming inside is speech of thought. That is the way the angels speak.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Likewise, the *Berachos* tractate speaks of two souls that spoke with each other. That communication is speech of thought, which a person does not hear, as explained elsewhere.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The second level is real thought: a person analyzes an idea such as G-d's rulership, thinking about its understanding, and the words of their thought are created by that analysis, to fit the understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The words of thought come out according to the *kavana* in the mind. That true, conscious thought is what we mean by thought: the *kavana* creates the words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Each of the three has two kinds. Action of thought can be passive, like a dream, triggered from outside, or a conscious visualizing that one holds and controls. Speech of thought can be words someone else says that call up letters in the mind, or words brought up without *kavana*. Real thought is analytical, *machshava iyunis*, creating words to help analyze the idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: (כמו שאנו רואים בצירופי אותיות המחשבה, שמתהווים רק כפי הכוונה שבשכל,
phrases.en: like we see, that the letters of thought are created according to the kavana in the mind

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: אם כך וכך יתהווה אופן הצירוף כך וכך וכידוע)
phrases.en: that the person's thoughts are going to come according to what they're thinking about and what they're understanding, and that *kavana* is creating the letters

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כמו אם כוונתו בשכל בענין דבר פרט לאיזה מסחור או בענין אדנות,
phrases.en: if a person in their *kavana* and their intellect they're focusing their mind's attention on a certain thing, for a business deal, or about G-d's kingship,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: They're going to think in different words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: a lot of times that happens, where a person's *kavana* creates a certain way of thinking, and that could be good, or bad, or neutral, but anyway, a person's *machshava* is created from their *kavana* when it's truly real thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: That's called real thought, thought of thought.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שהוא הנקרא כח המחשבה לחשוב כל ענין דבר מה בצירופים שונים
phrases.en: And this is the real power of thought, where a person can take their ideas and their understanding, and they can give them symbols in different words to express them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: Just like the power of speech is that you can express yourself in different to say whatever you want to say,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: you can also think whatever you want to think, but the real thought is when it's expressing something that's inside of you, an idea you have.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: like we will explain later

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.en: And so this power of thought is the vessel, is the tool that allows analytical thought

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: הנקרא מחשבת השכל עצמו (הנזכר לעיל באות מ׳) בחינת מלכות דתבונה כו'
phrases.en: which is called the thought of the *sechel* itself, like we talked about before in chapter 40, *Malchus* of *tevuna*, and this power is *Malchus* of *tevuna*, the ability to take an idea and create words to express that idea.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The letters of thought form only according to the *kavana* in the intellect. Focused on a business deal, or on G-d's kingship, a person thinks in different words, the ones that fit that focus.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So *ratzon* and *taanug* come out in how a person thinks: someone thinking about business sees his money, and someone whose priority is G-d sees *hashgacha pratis* and his *avoda*, when the same thing happens.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The chametz poured into the river
blocks.text: A man had a beer factory, or some sort of beverage factory. Before Pesach the townspeople, told by "the priest or something" not to buy his *chametz*, could not buy it, and he could not sell it. He declared the *chametz* ownerless and poured it into the river, leaving the barrels there. After the holiday he came back. The townspeople complained that they had not been able to get it, and wild animals had guarded it. He saw that G-d had made a great *nes*. But then he decided that perhaps he had not really given up ownership, so he poured it all out, to show he had no *chametz* on Pesach. A man thinking about business would have thought, "Great, I can get my money back." Someone whose main priority was G-d's mastery thought, "I should pour it out," and that is what he did.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The grandfather of a rebbe
blocks.text: He believes the man was the grandfather of a famous rebbe, maybe the *Chozeh* of Lublin, who merited very special descendants. He will not name the wrong one; clearly the man was a very special *neshama*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: What a person understands changes how they think and which words they use, so words matter. That is why propaganda frames a conversation in words built on assumptions, which are hard to challenge once one is inside the argument. The loaded question "Did you stop beating your wife yet?" is the example: yes or no, either answer accepts the assumption.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So a person's way of thinking is often created by their *kavana*, which can be good, bad or neutral. When it is truly real thought, a person's *machshava* is created from their *kavana*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This is called real thought, thought of thought: the power to take one's ideas and understanding and give them symbols in different words to express them, as one does in speech.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: As speech lets a person say whatever they want, thought lets them think whatever they want. Real thought expresses an idea one has inside, and that is where it is really called *machshava*; we will explain this about speech later.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: This power of thought is the vessel for analytical thought, the thought of the *sechel* itself, which we talked about in chapter 40 as *Malchus* of *tevuna*: the ability to take an idea and create words to express it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sections.title: Daas, and thought that is one's own
sections.summary: Thought depends on daas. A child has no thought of its own because it lacks understanding, and a grown person's thought is their own only when they take the idea in and express it in their own words.

phrases.en: And this type of thought depends on daas.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ולזה אמרו דקטן אין לו מחשבה, דלפי קטנות דעתו כך הוא קטנות המחשבה בלא צירופים כלל,
phrases.en: and this is why we say a katan doesn't have machshava, because they're immature, so their machshava is also immature

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: אבל גדלות הדעת הוא המביא למחשבה בריבוי צירופים שונים
phrases.en: when a person has maturity, and they have this mature daas

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: ולפי אופן העמקת הדעת בעומק המושג
phrases.en: And so the same thing, right?

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: כך יהיה עומק המחשבה בבחינת עומק מחשבה עיונית הנזכר לעיל

phrases.en: like it says, how deep are your thoughts, G-d,

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

phrases.he: שתלוי בערך עומק המושג דבינה כו'
phrases.en: that according to the depth of understanding, that's how much you can perceive the depth of thoughts.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Thought depends on *daas*. That is why a *katan* has no thought: lacking its own understanding, even a child told to think a certain *kavana* is not really having it. It may think the words, not the *kavana*, and that is why *halacha* says a child cannot do certain things.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A *katan* has no thought of its own, because its *daas* is immature, so its thought is immature too. It repeats what it was told, saying, "Oh, this, that," in words that are someone else's.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Kids can be very impressionable: you can get them all fired up to do things, and they never stop to think about it. You see that a lot these days with the youth. They get riled up, but this has always happened throughout history.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

sensitivity.reason: A generalisation about young people today, offered as a class remark; the public text keeps the point that impressionable people act without thinking and drops the remark about these days.
sensitivity.publishable: Kids can be very impressionable: you can get them all fired up to do things, and they never stop to think about it. They get riled up, but this has always happened throughout history.

blocks.text: With a mature *daas*, a person thinks in many combinations: they start to think about what they are doing and believing, and why, and form their own thoughts and opinions about it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same holds for G-d's unity. A person can say "*Shema Yisrael*" and know G-d is one, but if only trained to say it, that is not real mature belief. Real mature belief understands it and develops it: what does it mean that G-d is one? *Chovos HaLevavos*, in *Shaar HaYichud*, speaks of this.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: How deeply thought goes depends on how deeply one relates to the depth of the idea, the *hamshacha hadaas*. An idea only outside me, like words in a book, I understand in theory but cannot internalize or make my own words. With *hamshacha hadaas* I experience it personally, and that is *daas*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: Hearing that war is bad
blocks.text: It is not like being told that war is bad. I feel its pain and suffering; it is personally felt, I have real opinions, and I can think about it in my own words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same is true of G-d's unity and of love and fear of G-d. *Hamshacha hadaas* lets a person internalize it to the real depth, which brings the depth of *tevuna* and lets them create their own words. Putting it into your own words requires *hamshacha hadaas*, and practicing that develops it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So we should take our *emuna*, bring the *pnimiyus* to understand and express it, and personalize *mitzvos* with our own meaning and *kavana*, beyond the words we are told. Apply what we learn to all of life, and find a lesson in every *mitzva* and every part of Torah. That is where you get the depth, and the depth of thought matches the depth of understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: "How deep are your thoughts," as it says: the depth of thought depends on the depth of *bina*, and so on how much one can perceive. This is the general theme of *katnus* and *gadlus*: our awareness of G-dliness decides whether we perceive *hashgacha pratis* externally or in a real way.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Torah and mitzvos tell a person that everything comes from G-d as *hashgacha pratis*, and they can think those words without seeing it personally. When they really understand it, they see G-d's hand in everything, and that is real *machshava*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: The same with the *kavana* of the mitzvos: when a person really understands the *kavana* behind them, they can do them with true *machshava*, true depth. That is the idea of *kavana*.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: As it says in *Hayom Yom*, the *kavanos* of the Arizal should be thought in *davenen* only by one who really understands them; otherwise they are meaningless words. We give things names all the time, so we must train ourselves to ask what the words really mean.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: A person can say many words of *Chassidus* or *Kabbalah*, call this a level and that a level, and still not understand it at all; they have memorized and been trained to say the words.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: So we have to stop and think: what do those words really mean? Can I put it into my own words, instead of parroting the book? That is the sign that I internalize it.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.title: The Mitteler Rebbe's maamarim
blocks.text: The Alter Rebbe allowed only the Mitteler Rebbe to say over his *maamarim* in his own words; other *chassidim* had to repeat them word for word. I think he did not trust anyone else to understand them, and in their own words they would misrepresent them.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: We need humility: sometimes a thing must be said exactly as it was said, because there is a depth beyond our understanding. But we must also put it into our own words and go beyond parroting, so that we could write the book ourselves. Practicing that develops a deeper understanding.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Going back to the *nimshal*: if we view Torah and mitzvos as only external, just doing what G-d tells us, that is a state of *galus*. It is an important stage, but in the times of *Moshiach* the mitzvos will be *batel*. The Rebbe explains that this does not mean they will not be done; it means they will not be done as a mitzva commanded from outside, but because we feel this is who we are and what we want.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3

blocks.text: Then it comes from our own *kavana*, *machshava* and *ratzon*, not from speech or being told. So we relate to Torah and mitzvos personally, through *bina*. That is why *bina* is connected to freedom: real freedom comes from understanding, when we live Torah as connected to us personally.

audio.lecture: Walters 5784 Edited/041 Shaar HaYichud ch 41 enhanced.mp3
